key_insight: MOSAIC introduces a local, steerable atomistic representation that gives generative models persistent spatial addresses for controlling and assembling matter across molecular to million-atom scales.
engineering_relevance: This enables more controllable molecular design, scalable construction of heterogeneous materials, and bounded assembly workflows for large atomistic structures relevant to engineering applications.
method: Partition space into anchored regions with discrete atom slots.
Encode each slot with occupancy, species, and continuous displacement from its anchor.
Use the representation with different generative backbones for local conditioning and hierarchical generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved molecular connectivity and validity, efficient sampling across molecular sizes, fine-grained spatial control, and generation of atomistic polycrystals and structures with more than one million atoms.
watch_item: As a representation-only approach, performance still depends on the chosen generative backbone and on careful handling of slot/anchor resolution for different target scales.
paper_title: MOSAIC: Addressing Space for Local, Steerable, and Scalable Atomistic Generation
